note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: 3-day history of profuse diarrhea; likely infectious gastroenteritis (brother and others at school affected).
- Symptom timeline and progression: Onset 3 days ago; initially watery, now very loose; ≥4 bowel movements today; ongoing vomiting of all oral intake; subjective fever since onset.
- ENT symptoms: Denies throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling, ear pain/hearing changes, neck pain/swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: No similar prior episodes. Self-treatment with oral rehydration solution (home salt-sugar mix) three times daily for 2 days; no improvement.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Current medications: Vitamin D (dose/route/frequency not documented); occasional ibuprofen for dysmenorrhea (dose/route/frequency not documented); ORS as above.
- Social context: Lives with brother and mother; working from home due to illness; telephone consultation in private setting.

Objective:
- Observable swelling/distribution: Not recorded.
- Airway/breathing: No respiratory complaints; no stridor or dyspnea reported.
- Mental status/associated features: Alert; reports abdominal pain centered at umbilicus; no rash.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded (telephone consult).
- Accompaniment: Patient at home; no third party on the call.

Assessment:
- Likely infectious gastroenteritis with ongoing vomiting and risk of dehydration; no ENT involvement identified.

Plan:
- Arrange urgent clinic appointment for stool specimen collection and hydration assessment.
- Continue oral rehydration salts: very small, frequent sips.
- Dietary advice: bland/simple foods (e.g., toast, biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, milk.
- Escalation/red-flag advice: Attend A&E or call back urgently if worsening vomiting, inability to keep down fluids, reduced urine output, persistent high fever, dizziness, or any new breathing/throat symptoms.
- Follow-up: Patient to book appointment through support line; may call back if condition deteriorates before appointment.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing/expected elements: allergy list, vital signs, ENT physical examination, documentation of hydration status (mucous membranes, capillary refill), medication doses/routes/frequencies, assessment of auto-injector availability (not indicated but standard in severe allergic/ENT swelling scenarios).
● Internal conflicts: None identified.
● Transcript quality: Clear; occasional minor inaudible pauses but clinically non-impactful.
